articles.description: Orsted announced the start of commercial operation at the 704-megawatt Revolution Wind, a 50:50 partnership with GIP that was among several U.S. offshore wind projects threatened with cancelation by the Trump administration.

articles.title: America’s Nuclear Revival Is Running Into a Fuel Supply Wall
articles.description: The United States boasts the largest nuclear power production capacity in the world, but decades of insufficient funding and policy support is now posing an existential threat to the ageing sector. In the past decade, the United States has added just one new nuclear power plant to its fleet, while many more plants are drawing close to being decommissioned, at a time when clean, round-the-clock energy production has never been more needed. articles.title: Oil Traders Want U.S. to Release Sanctioned Tankers as Freight Costs Soar
articles.description: Some of the world's biggest oil traders are asking Washington for permission to put sanctioned tankers back to work, as a global vessel shortage pushes oil transportation costs to extraordinary levels. Trafigura, Vitol, Mercuria and Abu Dhabi National Oil Co. are negotiating with U.S. officials for licenses to purchase or lease blacklisted oil tankers, Bloomberg reported Friday, citing people familiar with the discussions. The talks involve approximately 50 vessels currently under U.S. sanctions. Treasury officials are considering approvals on…

articles.title: Energy Reliability Is Becoming More Important Than Energy Politics
articles.description: For much of the past decade, energy debates often pitted fossil fuels against clean energy. Governments announced dates for phasing out technologies, investors tried to anticipate which industries would lose favor, and energy policy increasingly became entangled with political identity. The war with Iran has exposed the limitations of approaching energy policy that way. When supplies are disrupted and prices rise sharply, governments become much less interested in ideological consistency and much more interested in keeping fuel available,…

articles.title: U.S. Oil, Gas Drillers See Minor Uptick as Oil Prices Crash
articles.description: The total number of active drilling rigs for oil and gas in the United States rose slightly this week, according to new data that Baker Hughes published on Friday, with the total rig count in the US rising to 604, up 56 from this same time last year. The number of active oil rigs rose by 1, to 463 during the latest reporting period, according to the data. This is 49 above this same time last year. articles.title: ONGC Posts Highest H1 Profit
articles.description: The Indian state-owned company reported around $3.46 billion in net income for the first half of its 2027 financial year, up 82 percent from the same six-month period of the prior year as high realized oil and gas prices offset lower production.

articles.title: ONGC Moves to Take Over Venezuelan Oilfields, Recover $500 Million
articles.description: India’s state-owned Oil and Natural Gas Corp. (ONGC) is negotiating to take over operations at two Venezuelan oil projects within six months, a move that could give it control over production and sales at fields where it is owed more than $500 million in dividends. The company's overseas arm, ONGC Videsh, is in advanced discussions with Venezuelan and U.S. authorities, finance chief Anupam Agarwal told analysts Friday. articles.title: Norway’s Oil and Gas Industry Faces a Major Decline Without New Discoveries
articles.description: For more than half a century, Norway’s oil and gas production has been underpinned by a handful of very large discoveries, the last of which, Wisting in the Barents Sea, was made more than a decade ago. Since then, exploration on the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS) has increasingly focused on smaller finds close to existing infrastructure, allowing operators to bring new volumes online faster and at lower cost. While this approach has helped sustain production in the near term, it will not be enough to arrest the NCS’s projected decline…

articles.title: Energy Aspects Slashes Forecast of China’s November Diesel Exports
articles.description: Reduced domestic inventories will likely result in significantly lower Chinese exports of diesel in November amid the global diesel crisis, analysts at Energy Aspects say as they slashed their estimates of Chinese shipments this month. Energy Aspects now sees China’s diesel exports at about 580,000 tons in November, down by 400,000 tons from the previous assessment, according to a note carried by Bloomberg. However, there could be upward revisions to the new forecast as refiners may ramp up shipments if domestic demand starts to drop off…

articles.description: Canadian pipeline operator TC Energy has announced approximately C$3bn ($2.1bn) of new in-corridor growth projects, taking 2026 sanctions to about C$6bn at a weighted average build multiple of 6.5 times.

articles.description: President Donald Trump spent the final weeks of the US midterm campaign predicting that the war with Iran would end "right after the election." With the votes now in, his Republican Party is reeling from losing both chambers of Congress in a rout that his own vice president blamed squarely on the conflict. "The reason we lost is the war," Vice President JD Vance wrote on X on November 4.
